Subject: MedSyst MAP: POC environment - auth & network checklist

Hi Alex / MedSyst team,

Per our MAP, lining up the POC environment tasks so we can hit the target close date (week of Jul 12). Short checklist below — could you confirm owners and ETA for each item by EOD tomorrow? I attached a working MAP spreadsheet and a quick network diagram.

- API keys: request for a dedicated API key per environment (staging-poc). We'll need an initial key scoped to evaluation traffic and a rotation plan.
- Redwood org invite: please add redwood-poc@medsyst.com (we'll provide the invite link) — this gives our runtime service account permissions to register the POC tenancy.
- IP allowlist: required for prefix-level egress to our hosted endpoints (see suggested CIDR ranges in the attached CSV). Please confirm the public egress IPs you can allow.
- VPC peering: confirm whether you prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink; if peering, share VPC CIDR, region, and a preferred maintenance window.

Key asks:
1) Confirm responsible contact for Procurement to process the POC contract (procurement@medsyst.com copied).
2) Provide the VPC CIDR and preferred peering window.
3) Confirm one admin for the API key request (name + email).

Attachments: MedSyst_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), network_diagram_vpc.png, medsyst_vpc_cidrs.csv

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if it helps.

—Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0193

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and a few clarifying Qs.

- API keys: Will assign to our cloud-admin team. Owner: Beth Carter (beth.carter@medsyst.com). Can you confirm the exact scopes you need? We generally prefer short-lived keys for evals.
- Org invite: happy to accept. Do you have a specific invite email to use for the service account?
- IP allowlist: attaching our outbound NAT CIDRs (medsyst_vpc_cidrs.csv) — we can allow those by tomorrow.
- VPC peering: Peering is fine. We are in us-west-2; VPC CIDR: 10.44.0.0/16. Preferred maintenance window: Sat 02:00–05:00 UTC. We need to know whether you require route table changes on our side or if the peering will be initiated from Redwood.

Follow-ups:
- Can Redwood provide a minimal inbound firewall rule set for debug ports (SSH to bastion only)?
- Any special headers or mTLS requirements for API calls during the POC?

I attached the CIDR export and looped procurement. If you can send a short doc on the peering steps, our infra lead will schedule the window.

—Alex

Alex — tagging in a few technical notes to make peering and key provisioning straightforward. Happy to run the peering with your infra team in the window you suggested.

Quick answers and steps:
1) API keys / scopes
   - Create a scoped token with these scopes: read:models, generate:text, manage:kvcache (for experimental caching). We can issue a short-lived token for eval usage if you prefer (recommended).
   - To create: MedSyst cloud-admin -> Redwood Console -> Admin -> API Keys -> Create key -> set \"Environment: staging-poc\". We will accept the key via secure upload or you can create and paste into the MAP spreadsheet.

2) Org invite / service account
   - Use invite address: redwood-poc+medsyst@redwood.inference.com. Once invited, we will register the org and create the initial POC tenancy. Please grant "Org Admin" to that invite temporarily; we will reduce permissions after setup.

3) VPC peering steps (us-west-2)
   - We will initiate the peering request from our side. Please add a route for 10.44.0.0/16 to the peering attachment and allow the following on your security group: TCP 443 to Redwood service endpoints, outbound to our NAT ranges (see attachment).
   - No inbound SSH required except to a bastion host for debugging. If you prefer, we can also use a short-lived temporary tunnel for the initial data sync.

4) Maintenance window and rollback
   - Proposed: Sat Jul 10, 02:00–05:00 UTC (so POC is ready well before your target week). We'll plan a 30-minute blackout for validation, then rollback instructions in the MAP doc.

Shared resources: Quick-start doc (link below) and a Drive folder with sample route table updates. I'll be on the call to assist.

Links: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/:f:/s/Enterprise/MedSystPOC?csf=1&web=1

—Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.inference.com
